ux.title: Install foo
ux.c: You double-click foo-setup.exe in your Downloads folder.
ux.s: Your normal Downloads folder. The installer says it's signed by foo.
ux.f: Nothing yet. Because the installer is signed and installs just for you, Windows doesn't ask for an admin password.

ux.title: Install foo
ux.c: The first installer screen asks one thing: should foo start when you sign in to Windows? It's already ticked.
ux.s: "Install foo" with one line about what foo is, a ticked box, and Install / Cancel.
ux.f: Waits for your tap. Installs only into your own user folder.

ux.title: Install foo
ux.c: You tap Install. A progress bar runs for about a minute.
ux.s: "Installing… this takes about a minute." and a bar. Nothing else to read.
ux.f: Copies foo, adds a Start menu shortcut and registers notifications.

ux.title: Install foo
ux.c: Near the end, foo quietly checks your PC is ready: Windows version, 2 GB free, Edge or Chrome, and that Documents isn't an online-only folder.
ux.s: The same progress bar, almost full. No questions.
ux.f: Runs the readiness check silently and only speaks up if something would stop it working.

ux.title: Install foo
ux.c: "foo is ready." foo opens by itself after 3 seconds, or you tap Open foo.
ux.s: The last installer screen, plus foo's "f" now in the taskbar and the tray.
ux.f: Starts foo hidden in the tray first, with the tooltip "foo · setting up".

ux.title: Install foo
ux.c: foo's window opens with a short "Starting…" screen.
ux.s: The foo wordmark in the middle of a plain window.
ux.f: Loads your (empty) chats and settings. Opens in under 2 seconds.

ux.title: Install foo
ux.c: The real window: one greyed "foo" row on the left and a welcome card in the middle.
ux.s: "Hi, I'm foo." with a single Let's go button. Underneath: "Nothing leaves this PC unless you say so."
ux.f: Nothing until you tap. The message box is locked until your AI is connected.

ux.title: Install foo
ux.c: If you close the window now, foo just tucks into the tray. Next time it opens on this same card.
ux.s: The foo icon by the clock, tooltip "foo · setting up".
ux.f: Saves where setup stopped, so you never start again from scratch.

ux.title: Find your AI
ux.c: foo looks for an AI you already have, in a fixed order: Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, saved keys, then a free AI on this PC.
ux.s: A card with five rows, each spinning "Looking…". A pill in the header says "Step 1 of 4".
ux.f: Checks your PC for sign-ins and saved keys. It doesn't install anything.

ux.title: Find your AI
ux.c: For each one it finds, foo asks one tiny real question, with 20 seconds to answer.
ux.s: Claude and ChatGPT say "Testing…". Gemini and a local AI aren't here. "OpenAI key" offers a secret box.
ux.f: Sends "Reply with the word ready" to each AI it found.

ux.title: Find your AI
ux.c: Both answered. Until one AI really works, the message box stays locked.
ux.s: Two green "✓ works". The message box reads "Connect your AI first, then we can talk."
ux.f: Keeps chat locked until a live test passes, so you never talk to a dead end.

ux.title: Find your AI
ux.c: foo picks the first one that works and tells you why, in one line.
ux.s: "I'll use Claude…" with Use Claude / Pick another, and a note that this uses your Claude plan.
ux.f: Picks Claude because it's first in the order and good at bookings. Waits for your tap.

ux.title: Find your AI
ux.c: You tap Use Claude. The card shrinks to one line and chat unlocks.
ux.s: "✓ Using Claude (your AI)". Details → Using shows "Claude (your AI)". The pill moves to "Step 2 of 4".
ux.f: Saves Claude as your AI. Your words go only to Claude, nowhere else.

ux.title: Find your AI
ux.c: What if foo finds no AI at all? It asks which one you use, or whether you have a key.
ux.s: "I couldn't find an AI on this PC yet. Which one do you use?" with sign-in choices and "I have a key".
ux.f: Links to the maker's own sign-in page. It never installs anything silently.

ux.title: Find your AI
ux.c: You pick "I have a key" → OpenAI. foo shows a Secret box, never a chat bubble, for the key.
ux.s: "To use your own AI I need your OpenAI key. Paste it in the box below, not in the chat." A masked box with Save securely.
ux.f: The key goes straight into Windows' own safe store. foo's AI only ever sees the name "OpenAI key".

ux.title: Find your AI
ux.c: What if you paste the key into the message box by mistake? foo stops it before it's sent.
ux.s: A warning card above the message box: "That looks like a key". The send button is greyed out.
ux.f: Spots the key pattern on your PC before anything leaves. Offers to move it to the Secret box.

ux.title: Find your AI
ux.c: Saved. With a key, foo shows cost and stops at your monthly cap, ₹1,000 to start. (Vikas had Claude, so the rest uses Claude.)
ux.s: "✓ Saved securely. foo's AI never sees it." and "OpenAI key ✓ works", with a line about the ₹1,000 cap.
ux.f: Tests the key with one real question, then turns on the AI spend meter.

ux.title: Name and face
ux.c: foo asks what to call itself. It never suggests a name in its own words.
ux.s: "What should I call myself?" with an empty box, Keep "foo" and 🎲 Surprise me.
ux.f: Waits. The only source of name ideas is the dice button.

ux.title: Name and face
ux.c: You tap 🎲 and it fills "Juno". Tap again for another, or keep your own.
ux.s: "Juno" in the box, with That's it, Keep "foo" and 🎲.
ux.f: Picks from a built-in list of 200 short names, never repeating in one go.

ux.title: Name and face
ux.c: Vikas keeps "foo". It answers in three words.
ux.s: The card shrinks to "What should I call myself? → foo", then "foo it is."
ux.f: Saves the name. If you'd picked Juno, the chat list, header and notifications would change within a second.

ux.title: Name and face
ux.c: "Pick a face." foo's living face comes first and is already picked. You can still choose another face or your own picture.
ux.s: Four round faces: foo's two eyes on its black disc, marked "Living face (default)", then ✿, ◐ and ★. Buttons for new faces or your own picture.
ux.f: If your AI can make pictures, the other three would be fresh ones; otherwise these presets. A picture or emoji you choose is never changed.

ux.title: Name and face
ux.c: You keep the living face. The header and the chat row show it straight away, blinking now and then.
ux.s: A ring around the chosen face. The left row is no longer grey, and the same two eyes sit in the header.
ux.f: Uses the face in the chat list, header, notifications and tray. The app icon keeps the "f".

ux.title: Name and face
ux.c: foo shows you once how to read its face.
ux.s: "My face shows what I'm really doing." Four small faces: a turning blue ring = working · an amber ring = needs you · smiling eyes = done · closed eyes = quiet hours.
ux.f: The face only changes when something really happens: a job, a card, the internet or the clock. With a picture face, the same news shows as a thin ring around it.

ux.title: Name and face
ux.c: "How should I talk to you?" You choose a vibe.
ux.s: A choice card: Calm, a bit funny (Best fit) · Straight to the point · Warm and chatty · Something else…
ux.f: Tone only. It never changes what foo is allowed to do.

ux.title: Name and face
ux.c: You can also just type your answer. While you type, foo's eyes look down toward the message box.
ux.s: "calm, a bit funny" in the message box. In the header, foo's eyes have moved down and blink slowly.
ux.f: Notices only that you're typing, never what. The eyes look back up 5 seconds after you stop.

ux.title: Name and face
ux.c: One line back, in that voice. The pill moves to Step 3 of 4.
ux.s: "Calm, a bit funny. Got it. 🌿"
ux.f: Saves the vibe. Settings → Chat and voice can change it later.

ux.title: Name and face
ux.c: What if your first message is a real job? foo does that first, then comes back to setup.
ux.s: You typed "remind me to call Rohit at 9 PM". foo answers, then "Now, back to my name…"
ux.f: Your request always comes first. Setup resumes right after.

ux.title: Quick interview and connections
ux.c: Eight short questions, one card each. First: what should foo call you?
ux.s: "What should I call you?" with a "Vikas" chip from your Windows account, Something else… and Skip.
ux.f: Offers your Windows name as a chip. Your AI doesn't see it unless you pick it.

ux.title: Quick interview and connections
ux.c: "Hi Vikas." Next: may foo peek at which apps you have? Not your files.
ux.s: "Can I peek at which apps you have installed? Not your files." Yes, have a look / No thanks.
ux.f: If yes, reads only the list of installed apps, to pre-tick the next card.

ux.title: Quick interview and connections
ux.c: Which apps do you use most? foo pre-ticked what it saw. You tap Done.
ux.s: Chips: WhatsApp ✓ · Gmail + Calendar ✓ · Outlook · X ✓ · Instagram · None of these.
ux.f: Notes X for drafting later. Posting is never done by foo.

ux.title: Quick interview and connections
ux.c: Gmail and Calendar: a Connect card says exactly what foo will and won't do.
ux.s: "Connect Gmail and Calendar. I'll read emails and your calendar to spot bills, trips and plans. I'll write drafts, but I never send without your tap."
ux.f: Nothing yet. Connect opens Google's own sign-in in your normal browser.

ux.title: Quick interview and connections
ux.c: Google's own page opens in your browser. You check what foo asks for and allow it.
ux.s: Read email · create drafts · send only after you approve in foo · see and add calendar events.
ux.f: Waits. foo never sees your Google password.

ux.title: Quick interview and connections
ux.c: Back in foo: connected. Details → Using now shows Gmail and Calendar.
ux.s: "✓ Connected as v••••@gmail.com".
ux.f: Saves the connection in Windows' safe store. Starts reading only what it needs.

ux.title: Quick interview and connections

ux.f: Nothing until you tap Show QR code.

ux.c: Scan the code with your phone, like linking WhatsApp on a computer.
ux.s: A QR code and three numbered lines: open WhatsApp → Linked devices → point your phone here.
ux.f: Waits for the phone to link. Read and draft only; sending always needs your tap.

ux.title: Quick interview and connections

ux.title: Quick interview and connections

ux.f: Saves it as "You said", dated today, in plain files on your PC.

ux.title: Quick interview and connections
ux.c: Brief time, then how much foo may do alone. "Check with me first" is the default.
ux.s: "When should I send your morning brief?" → 8:00 AM. "How much should I do on my own?" Check with me first (Best fit) · Go ahead with small things.
ux.f: Even "small things" never means sending, buying, booking, posting or deleting without a card.

ux.title: Quick interview and connections
ux.c: foo sums up what it learned in one message and asks you to fix anything.
ux.s: "Here's what I've got, Vikas: you use Gmail, Calendar and WhatsApp · Mom's birthday is 18 Oct · morning brief at 8:00 AM. Fix anything?"
ux.f: Shows its notes before relying on them. The pill will move to Step 4 of 4.

ux.title: First real job, inside a minute

ux.s: Chips: Find bills due this week · Spot my upcoming trips · What's on this week? · Anything I missed in chats?
ux.f: Offers only jobs it can really do with your connections.

ux.title: First real job, inside a minute
ux.c: You tap the first chip. It becomes your message, with 👀 within a second.
ux.s: Your dark bubble "Find bills due this week" with a 👀 badge.

ux.title: First real job, inside a minute
ux.c: A checklist appears within 2 seconds and ticks itself off. Your badge turns to 🛠.
ux.s: ✓ Reading your Gmail (last 30 days) · ◌ Looking for bills and due dates · ○ Checking your calendar for trips.

ux.title: First real job, inside a minute

ux.f: Shows "done" only because it has proof: the three emails it read. foo's very first job, so its face celebrates once, with a few sparks.

ux.title: First real job, inside a minute

ux.s: Looks right · Change something · Take it further.

ux.title: First real job, inside a minute

ux.title: First real job, inside a minute

ux.s: "☀ Good morning, Vikas": Mom's birthday · Airtel bill · Goa prices · weather. Each line has at most one button and 👍 👎. "That's all for today."

ux.title: Morning brief

ux.title: Morning brief

ux.title: Morning brief

ux.s: "What I know about you": Allergic to peanuts · Likes beach stays · Budget trips under ₹40,000 · See all (25).
ux.f: Each line says "You said" or "I guessed".

ux.title: Memory you can see and forget
ux.c: The full page (Ctrl+M): every fact, where it came from, and when.
ux.s: Filters All · You said · I guessed · People · From Gmail · From WhatsApp. Rows with Edit · Forget · Mark private.
ux.f: Memory is plain files on your PC. Nothing is hidden.

ux.title: Memory you can see and forget
ux.c: Filter to "I guessed" to check foo's guesses.
ux.s: Only "Prefers window seats · from 4 bookings" and "Mom's birthday · From Gmail".
ux.f: Shows the reason for every guess.

ux.title: Memory you can see and forget
ux.c: Correct things by just saying them. Old facts are replaced, not piled up.
ux.s: "actually I moved to Pune" → "Updated: you live in Pune (was Mumbai)." with Undo.
ux.f: Updates the fact and its date.

ux.title: Memory you can see and forget
ux.c: Forget one thing. It disappears with a 5-second Undo.
ux.s: The window-seats row is gone. A bar: "Forgot 'Prefers window seats' · Undo".
ux.f: Won't use it again, or re-learn it from the same bookings, for 90 days.

ux.title: Memory you can see and forget
ux.c: Forget everything from one source, with a count.
ux.s: "Forget 23 things I learned from your Gmail? Gmail stays connected; I just forget what I learned." Forget 23 things · Keep them.
ux.f: Leaves the Gmail connection alone.

ux.title: Memory you can see and forget
ux.c: Forget everything needs you to type FORGET.
ux.s: "This deletes everything I know about you, including helpers' notes. Your chats stay. Type FORGET to confirm."
ux.f: The button only works once the word matches.

ux.title: Memory you can see and forget
ux.c: "Open the memory folder" shows the plain files. Edit one in Notepad and foo uses it next reply.
ux.s: about-you.md in Notepad: simple lines like "- Allergic to peanuts (you said, Fri 16 Oct)".
ux.f: No hidden database: your memory is yours to read.

ux.title: Groups, and what stays private
ux.c: Start a group from the ⋯ next to "+ New helper" → New group.
ux.s: "New group": Name "Goa trip" · Members: Trips ✓ Money ✓ Home · foo · Create group · Not now.
ux.f: A group is you plus 2–6 helpers. foo can join too.

ux.title: Groups, and what stays private
ux.c: The group appears with stacked faces. The first helper you ticked opens it.
ux.s: "Goa trip" row. "Trips here with Money. Tell us what you need for Goa."
ux.f: Trips owns jobs here unless you @mention someone else.

ux.title: Groups, and what stays private
ux.c: You ask for something that needs two helpers.
ux.s: "plan dinner Saturday for the 6 of us and split the cost".
ux.f: Picks one owner for the job and hands the money part to Money.

ux.title: Groups, and what stays private
ux.c: One owner speaks, and the handoff is visible.
ux.s: "Trips: I'll find the place. Money will work out the split." · "Trips asked Money to work out the split".
ux.f: Only one helper owns each job.

ux.title: Groups, and what stays private
ux.c: Choices can be answered in the group.
ux.s: "Dinner on Sat 12 Dec: Fisherman's Wharf at 8:00 PM, table for 6?" Book it (Best fit) · Another place.
ux.f: Shows only plain text, choices and files in groups.

ux.title: Groups, and what stays private
ux.c: You tap Book it. The approval moves to your private chat with Trips.
ux.s: Amber line: "Trips: The booking and your phone number stay private. I've asked Vikas in his own chat." · Open Trips.
ux.f: Approvals, payments, drafts, sign-ins and personal details never appear in a group.

ux.title: Groups, and what stays private
ux.c: In Trips' own chat: the real Approval card.
ux.s: "Book this table?" Fisherman's Wharf, Sat 12 Dec, 8:00 PM · 6 people · Booked under Vikas Sharma · +91 98••• ••210 · Book table · Not now.
ux.f: Same rules as any booking: a tap, then a second look.

ux.title: Groups, and what stays private
ux.c: The group gets only the shareable result.
ux.s: "Trips: Booked. Fisherman's Wharf, Sat 12 Dec, 8:00 PM, table for 6. ✓ #FW-2201" · "Money: ₹1,450 each for 6 people (estimate)."
ux.f: Keeps your phone number and payment details out of the group.

ux.title: Groups, and what stays private
ux.c: Your WhatsApp Family group shows read-only. foo can draft into it; you send.
ux.s: Family group with a WhatsApp mark. A Draft: "Will send to Family group (8 people) from your WhatsApp. Can't be unsent." Send message.
ux.f: Helpers never post in WhatsApp groups by themselves.

ux.title: Groups, and what stays private
ux.c: If helpers go back and forth 6 times without you, the group pauses.
ux.s: "We're going in circles. Pausing until you reply."
ux.f: Stops runaway chatter and AI cost.

ux.title: Search everything (Ctrl+K)
ux.c: Ctrl+K opens one search box over everything.
ux.s: "Search chats, messages, files, routines, memory, settings" with filter chips.
ux.f: Searches on your PC only. Nothing goes to your AI.

ux.title: Search everything (Ctrl+K)
ux.c: Type "taj". Results appear grouped, in a blink.
ux.s: Messages: foo · "…book the Taj for Sat 12–Mon 14 Dec…" · Jobs: Goa stay · Done · Files: Taj-booking.pdf · What I know: Likes beach stays.
ux.f: Shows results after 2 letters, under a third of a second.

ux.title: Search everything (Ctrl+K)
ux.c: Enter opens the chat at that exact message, highlighted for 2 seconds.
ux.s: Trips' chat, the "Booked. Taj Holiday Village…" bubble glowing.
ux.f: Jumps without loading anything new.

ux.title: Search everything (Ctrl+K)
ux.c: Ctrl+Enter asks foo instead. Only then do your words go to your AI.
ux.s: "What did I book in Goa?" answered in foo's chat, with source pills you can click.
ux.f: Answers from your own chats and files, and shows where each fact came from.

ux.title: Search everything (Ctrl+K)
ux.c: The chips above the chat list filter it. "Needs you" shows only what's waiting on you.
ux.s: Only the Money row, with its amber "Needs you".
ux.f: Counts come from the real jobs.

ux.title: Search everything (Ctrl+K)
ux.c: Ctrl+F finds words inside the open chat.
ux.s: A "Find in this chat" bar: "rent", 1 of 3, ↑ ↓.
ux.f: Highlights each match in turn.

ux.title: Notifications, taskbar and tray
ux.c: The first time you close the window, foo explains it keeps working.
ux.s: "foo keeps working in the background. So it can do your jobs, routines and morning brief. You'll find foo in the tray, next to the clock." Got it · Quit foo instead · "Don't show again" ticked.
ux.f: Closing never quits foo unless you choose to.

ux.title: Notifications, taskbar and tray
ux.c: foo lives in the tray. Hover it to see what it's doing.
ux.s: Tooltip "foo · 2 jobs running". The taskbar button shows a thin green progress line.
ux.f: Keeps your PC from sleeping only while a job is working.

ux.title: Notifications, taskbar and tray
ux.c: A payment needs you. The notification can only open the card, never pay.
ux.s: "foo · Trips · Pay Taj Holiday Village ₹14,600?" Review · Not now. The taskbar "f" gets an amber "!".
ux.f: No secrets, card numbers or codes in notifications. At most one per chat every 2 minutes.

ux.title: Notifications, taskbar and tray
ux.c: Review opens foo right at the card, ready for your tap.
ux.s: Trips' chat with the Payment card focused.
ux.f: The approval itself only ever happens inside foo's window.

ux.title: Notifications, taskbar and tray
ux.c: A normal reply can be answered right from the notification.
ux.s: "foo · Trips · Want me to add the return flight too?" with a small reply box: "yes, Mon 14 Dec evening".
ux.f: Quick replies are just messages, so they're allowed.

ux.title: Notifications, taskbar and tray
ux.c: Right-click the tray icon for the essentials.
ux.s: Open foo · Needs you (1) · Doing now: Goa stay · step 3 of 4 · Pause routines until 10:00 AM, Fri 16 Oct · Quiet until… · Stop everything… · Settings · Quit foo.
ux.f: Every time in the menu is a real date and time.

ux.title: Notifications, taskbar and tray
ux.c: Quiet hours start at 10:00 PM. foo and its helpers close their eyes, and nothing pops up.
ux.s: 11:30 PM. Closed eyes and a small "z" on foo, Trips, Money and Home, in the chat list and the header. The tray face has its eyes closed too: "foo · quiet until 7:00 AM".
ux.f: Holds notifications until 7:00 AM. A job that is still running keeps its face awake, with the turning blue ring.

ux.title: Notifications, taskbar and tray
ux.c: During quiet hours (10:00 PM–7:00 AM) notifications wait, then come as one summary.
ux.s: Sat 17 Oct, 7:00 AM: "While you were away: 1 thing needs you, 2 jobs done."
ux.f: Respects Windows Focus too, and adds nothing on top. At 7:00 AM the faces open their eyes again.

ux.title: Notifications, taskbar and tray
ux.c: When a job finishes, the taskbar shows a green tick for 30 minutes.
ux.s: "Booked: Taj Holiday Village, Sat 12–Mon 14 Dec. ₹14,600 paid." and a green ✓ on foo's taskbar button.
ux.f: Plain unread messages never badge the taskbar.

ux.title: Notifications, taskbar and tray
ux.c: Right-click foo in the taskbar for quick tasks. No counts there, ever.
ux.s: New message to foo · Search · Stop everything · Settings.
ux.f: Same four tasks every time.

ux.title: Notifications, taskbar and tray
ux.c: Quitting with jobs running asks first, and nothing is paid while foo is closed.
ux.s: "Quit foo? 2 jobs are running. They'll pause and pick up when you open foo again. Nothing will be paid while foo is closed." Quit · Keep running.
ux.f: Saves every job. It never blocks Windows from shutting down.

ux.title: Spend caps you can always see
ux.c: Two meters are always in the Details panel: your AI and your purchases.
ux.s: "Your AI ₹212 of ₹1,000" and "Purchases ₹15,779 of ₹25,000".
ux.f: Counts every AI request and every payment as it happens.

ux.title: Spend caps you can always see
ux.c: At 80% of the AI cap, the meter turns amber and foo says so once.
ux.s: "Your AI ₹800 of ₹1,000" in amber. In chat: "You've used ₹800 of your ₹1,000 AI cap this month." · "Why am I getting this?"
ux.f: One line, not a notification.

ux.title: Spend caps you can always see
ux.c: At 100% everything stops. Not an alert: a hard stop.
ux.s: Banner: "You've reached this month's AI cap. 2 jobs paused." Card: "I've paused 2 jobs and 4 routines. Nothing was lost." Raise cap · "Wait until Sun 1 Nov".
ux.f: Pauses jobs and routines where they are.

ux.title: Spend caps you can always see
ux.c: Raise cap asks how much, right in the card.
ux.s: "New cap for October" ₹1,500 · ₹2,000 · Custom.
ux.f: A plain confirm, no hunting in Settings.

ux.title: Spend caps you can always see
ux.c: "Done. Picking up where I left off."
ux.s: The card edits itself to say so. The meter reads ₹1,000 of ₹1,500. The banner is gone.
ux.f: Resumes the paused jobs from the same step.

ux.title: Spend caps you can always see
ux.c: The purchase cap works the same way. A payment that would pass it never becomes a Payment card.
ux.s: In Trips: "This would pass your purchase cap. ₹15,779 spent of ₹25,000. This is ₹12,400." Raise cap · Not now.
ux.f: The job waits until you decide.

ux.title: Spend caps you can always see
ux.c: Big jobs show their cost up front.
ux.s: Plan card: "About 25 minutes · uses about ₹240 of your AI · This is a big one." Start job · Change plan.
ux.f: Any job that alone would use over 20% of your cap says so first.

ux.title: Spend caps you can always see
ux.c: The Spending page shows where it all went this month.
ux.s: Two tiles (AI and Purchases), AI by chat, AI by routine, and each purchase.
ux.f: Adds it up from the activity log; nothing is guessed.

ux.title: When things go wrong
ux.c: The internet drops. One strip under the title bar says what happened and what's safe.
ux.s: "You're offline. Your jobs are saved and I'll carry on when you're back." · Try again. The message box reads "You're offline. I'll send when you're back."
ux.f: Pauses jobs where they are. Your chats and memory still open.

ux.title: When things go wrong
ux.c: Anything you type is kept and sent when you're back.
ux.s: Your bubble with a small clock instead of ticks.
ux.f: Never loses a typed message.

ux.title: When things go wrong
ux.c: Back online: the error edits itself, and the job carries on from the same step.
ux.s: The strip is gone. The checklist ticks again; your message gets ✓✓.
ux.f: Re-tests every 30 seconds while offline.

ux.title: When things go wrong
ux.c: Your AI stops answering. Jobs wait; nothing is lost or paid.
ux.s: "Claude isn't answering right now. Your Goa job is saved at step 3. Nothing was booked or paid." · Try again · "Use ChatGPT instead".
ux.f: Offers ChatGPT only because it passed its test at setup.

ux.title: When things go wrong
ux.c: Plan limit reached? Paused until it resets. Plain chat can still get a short answer.
ux.s: "You've hit your Claude plan's limit until Fri 16 Oct, 3:00 PM. Your jobs are paused, not lost." · Remind me at 3:00 PM. A reply marked "answered with ChatGPT while Claude rests".
ux.f: Never uses the backup AI for jobs that send, buy or book.

ux.title: When things go wrong
ux.c: Stuck for 3 minutes? The real job runner says so, with the cost so far.
ux.s: "I'm stuck on the Goa job. What's wrong: MakeMyTrip keeps sending me back to the search page. Spent so far: about ₹6 of your AI · 9 minutes. What I'd do: try Booking.com instead." Try another way · Stop · Take over.
ux.f: No answer for 15 minutes → it stops and reports, fail-safe.

ux.title: When things go wrong
ux.c: foo crashed mid-payment. On restart it checks first, and never pays twice.
ux.s: "I closed unexpectedly at 9:42 AM. I was in the middle of paying ₹14,600. Checking whether it went through before anything else."
ux.f: Looks for the confirmation email and the bank's page. Never re-submits by itself.

ux.title: When things go wrong
ux.c: It went through, so foo says so and stops there.
ux.s: "It went through: booking #TJ88213. I didn't pay again." with proof.
ux.f: If it hadn't gone through, you'd get a fresh Payment card to approve.

ux.title: When things go wrong
ux.c: Any other unfinished job gets a recovery card. Your half-typed message is back too.
ux.s: "I closed unexpectedly at 9:42 AM. Delhi flights was at step 2 of 4. Nothing was paid." Pick up where I left off · Stop it. The message box still has "also check Akasa".
ux.f: Missed routines get one catch-up run each, not eight.

ux.title: When things go wrong
ux.c: Three crashes in 10 minutes: safe mode holds everything so nothing runs twice.
ux.s: "foo had trouble starting. I've paused everything so nothing runs twice." Start normally · Send a report.
ux.f: "Send a report" only saves a file on your PC and opens the folder. Nothing is uploaded.

ux.title: When things go wrong
ux.c: Smaller problems get one line and one fixing button.
ux.s: "Your Gmail connection expired. Bills and drafts are on hold." Reconnect · "WhatsApp unlinked foo." Link again · "irctc.co.in won't let me in. Nothing was booked." Open the page myself.
ux.f: Says "Nothing was booked, paid or sent" only when the activity log proves it.

ux.title: Settings, by page or by asking
ux.c: The gear at the bottom of the chat list opens Settings (or Ctrl+,).
ux.s: The ⚙ next to "Vikas · Claude ready".
ux.f: Opens on the last page you used.

ux.title: Settings, by page or by asking
ux.c: Account & your AI: which AI foo uses, and a live test button.
ux.s: "Using: Claude (your AI) · ✓ works · checked 2 min ago" · Test now · Change. Backup AI: ChatGPT.
ux.f: Test now sends one tiny real question.

ux.title: Settings, by page or by asking
ux.c: Permissions: Always · Ask · Never for each kind of action. Some can never be "Always".
ux.s: Pay, Send, Book, Delete and Share my address or phone have "Always" greyed. Hover it: "I'll always ask before paying."
ux.f: The lock is built in, not a setting you can lose.

ux.title: Settings, by page or by asking
ux.c: Asking foo to unlock it gets a straight answer.
ux.s: "let yourself pay without asking" → "Paying always needs your tap. That one can't change."
ux.f: No rule, setting or message can turn that off.

ux.title: Settings, by page or by asking
ux.c: Money: the two caps, Windows Hello for payments of ₹10,000 or more, and your cards and UPI.
ux.s: Monthly purchase cap ₹25,000 · Monthly AI cap ₹1,000 · "Confirm with Windows Hello for payments of at least ₹10,000" · Visa ••4242 (Default) · UPI.
ux.f: Hello can be lowered to ₹0 (every payment) but never turned off.

ux.title: Settings, by page or by asking
ux.c: Notifications: quiet hours, brief time, and at most 3 messages a day that foo starts itself.
ux.s: Quiet hours 10:00 PM – 7:00 AM · Morning brief 8:00 AM · "Up to 3 a day".
ux.f: Every message foo starts on its own carries "Why am I getting this?"

ux.title: Settings, by page or by asking
ux.c: Or just ask: "turn off voice replies". foo shows the changed setting with Undo.
ux.s: A mini card: "Voice replies: Never (was When I send voice)" · Undo.
ux.f: Changes it and logs the change in the Activity log.

ux.title: Settings, by page or by asking
ux.c: The Chat and voice page shows the same change.
ux.s: Voice replies: When I send voice · Always · Never (on). Hold to talk key: Ctrl+Space.
ux.f: One source of truth for every setting.

ux.title: Settings, by page or by asking
ux.c: Appearance follows Windows by default: light or dark, text size up to 225%, high contrast.
ux.s: Theme: Light · Dark · Windows. "Use my Windows accent colour" off.
ux.f: Works with Narrator and the keyboard everywhere.

ux.title: Settings, by page or by asking
ux.c: Connections: each app in one line, with one button to disconnect or unlink.
ux.s: Gmail ✓ connected · Calendar · WhatsApp linked · X drafts only · Outlook coming later · Signed-in sites (6).
ux.f: Disconnecting keeps what foo learned unless you forget it in Memory.

ux.title: Settings, by page or by asking
ux.c: Keyboard shortcuts, all on one page (Ctrl+/).
ux.s: Ctrl+K search · Ctrl+J jump to the card that needs you · Ctrl+M memory · Ctrl+R routines · Ctrl+H activity log…
ux.f: Esc closes the top thing but never declines a card.

ux.title: Settings, by page or by asking
ux.c: Updates download quietly and wait for you. foo never restarts by itself.
ux.s: A strip: "A new version of foo is ready." · Restart foo. About page: "What's new with me".
ux.f: Refuses to restart while a payment is in progress.

ux.title: Activity log, export, delete, uninstall
ux.c: The Activity log (Ctrl+H) lists everything foo sent, paid, booked, stopped or changed.
ux.s: Today: Paid ₹14,600 to Taj Holiday Village · Sent an email to Rakesh Sharma · Booked Pizza by the Bay · Stopped "Delhi flights" · Paid ₹1,179 to Airtel. Proof chips on each.
ux.f: Built only from what really happened, never from what the AI said.

ux.title: Activity log, export, delete, uninstall
ux.c: Privacy says in one sentence what leaves your PC.
ux.s: "Your messages and job details go to your AI (Claude). Sites you ask me to use see what you'd send them yourself. Nothing else leaves this PC. foo never uses your data to train anything."
ux.f: No foo account, no foo cloud.

ux.title: Activity log, export, delete, uninstall
ux.c: Export everything: you pick a folder, foo writes one zip.
ux.s: "Exporting… 40%" with a bar under the row.
ux.f: Includes chats, memory, routines and the activity log. Never keys, passwords or cards.

ux.title: Activity log, export, delete, uninstall
ux.c: Done, with the exact place it saved to.
ux.s: "Saved to Documents › foo-export-16-Oct-2026.zip. Keys and passwords aren't included." · Show in folder.
ux.f: Works even while jobs are running.

ux.title: Activity log, export, delete, uninstall
ux.c: Delete everything (inside foo) needs you to type DELETE.
ux.s: "Delete everything foo has on this PC? Chats, memory, routines, helpers, saved logins, cards and keys. Your Gmail, Calendar and WhatsApp will be disconnected. Files in Documents\foo stay. This can't be undone."
ux.f: The button only works once DELETE is typed.

ux.title: Activity log, export, delete, uninstall
ux.c: foo wipes itself and starts fresh at the welcome card.
ux.s: One greyed "foo" row and "Hi, I'm foo." again.
ux.f: Stopped jobs, signed out of Google and WhatsApp, cleared Windows' safe store, deleted its folder.

ux.title: Activity log, export, delete, uninstall
ux.c: Or uninstall from Windows: Settings → Apps → foo → Uninstall.
ux.s: Windows' Installed apps list, foo's ⋯ menu open on Uninstall.
ux.f: Windows starts foo's own uninstaller.

ux.title: Activity log, export, delete, uninstall
ux.c: The uninstaller asks what happens to your data. "Delete everything" is the default.
ux.s: Keep my data on this PC · Delete everything (selected): "Chats, memory, routines, saved logins, cards and keys are erased. Your Gmail, Calendar and WhatsApp connections are disconnected."
ux.f: Defaults to deleting, so secrets never outlive the app.

ux.title: Activity log, export, delete, uninstall
ux.c: Jobs still running? It warns you, and nothing will be paid.
ux.s: "2 jobs are still running. Uninstalling stops them. Nothing will be paid." Stop and uninstall · Cancel.
ux.f: Stops jobs cleanly and withdraws approvals.

ux.title: Activity log, export, delete, uninstall
ux.c: Last chance to keep a copy.
ux.s: "This can't be undone. Want a copy first? Export everything".
ux.f: Runs the same export as Settings, then continues.

ux.title: Activity log, export, delete, uninstall
ux.c: Removing foo, in a fixed order.
ux.s: "Removing foo…" with a bar: "Signing foo out of Google and WhatsApp…"
ux.f: Stop jobs → disconnect apps → clear saved logins, cards and keys → delete foo's folder → remove shortcuts.

ux.title: Activity log, export, delete, uninstall
ux.c: Done. Your own files are kept.
ux.s: "foo is removed. Your files in Documents\foo were kept. Your Claude account is untouched." · Close.
ux.f: No survey, no web page, nothing left behind.

ux.title: Activity log, export, delete, uninstall
ux.c: If you'd chosen "Keep my data", reinstalling picks up exactly where you left off.
ux.s: "foo is removed. Your data is kept on this PC. Reinstall foo to pick up where you left off."
ux.f: Skips setup next time if your AI still passes its test.
